title: Remote Connectivity, Host Modes, And Orchestrator Collapse
objective: Absorb orchestrator control-plane behavior into Server V2, route remote workspace behavior through the local server registry, and reduce any remaining host shell responsibilities to the thinnest possible layer.

steps.name: Inventory the remaining orchestrator control surfaces
steps.description: Turn the orchestrator audit into a concrete checklist of daemon APIs, runtime control routes, status surfaces, and CLI wrappers that still need to move behind Server V2.
successFactors: There is a concrete migration list for remaining orchestrator-owned product behavior.
The list distinguishes true host-shell needs from product control-plane debt.
Open questions are recorded if ownership is still ambiguous.

steps.name: Implement server-owned workspace activation routes
steps.description: Add Server V2 replacements for daemon workspace activation behavior so workspace lifecycle moves onto the main server API surface.
successFactors: Workspace activation is available through Server V2.
The server updates its own registry and runtime state when activation occurs.
Clients no longer need a separate daemon API for this capability.

steps.name: Implement server-owned workspace disposal routes
steps.description: Add Server V2 replacements for instance disposal or workspace shutdown behavior so runtime cleanup is also part of the main server API.
successFactors: Workspace disposal runs through the server.
The route updates runtime and registry state consistently.
The app and CLI can stop calling daemon disposal endpoints.

steps.name: Move runtime control semantics under `/system/runtime/*`
steps.description: Absorb legacy runtime versions, upgrade, and related control semantics into Server V2 under the normalized system namespace.
successFactors: Runtime control lives under the main server API.
Legacy route names are replaced or shimmed intentionally.
The route family aligns with the architecture plan.

steps.name: Implement runtime upgrade behavior in Server V2
steps.description: Move upgrade-related logic or the main product-facing upgrade route behind Server V2 so runtime inspection and upgrade are not orchestrator-owned product APIs anymore.
successFactors: Upgrade flows are server-owned or clearly proxied through the server.
The server can report upgrade status and errors consistently.
Later cutover can remove the legacy runtime control server.

steps.name: Implement remote server connection services
steps.description: Add the server-owned services and routes that register remote OpenWork servers, store connection metadata, and validate connectivity for remote workspaces.
successFactors: Remote server connections are stored in the server DB.
Connection validation happens through the local server, not the app alone.
The model supports remote and cloud-hosted OpenWork servers.

steps.name: Implement remote workspace discovery and sync
steps.description: Teach the local server to discover or refresh remote workspace metadata from configured remote servers and maintain the local canonical mapping in its registry.
successFactors: Remote workspace discovery is server-owned.
The local server stores remote workspace mappings durably.
The app can remain workspace-first even for remote content.

steps.name: Route remote workspace operations through the local server
steps.description: Ensure session, file, and other workspace-scoped operations for remote workspaces route through the local server as the canonical adapter instead of bypassing it from the app.
successFactors: The UI talks to the local server even for remote workspaces in normal product flows.
Remote backend IDs stay server-owned.
The local server remains the canonical registry and policy layer.

steps.name: Update CLI wrappers to target Server V2
steps.description: Move any thin orchestrator CLI wrappers for status, files, approvals, or runtime operations onto the main server API surface so the CLI does not preserve a separate control plane by accident.
successFactors: CLI wrappers call Server V2 routes.
The CLI no longer depends on daemon-only APIs for product behavior.
Any remaining host-shell CLI concerns are clearly separated.

steps.name: Shrink orchestrator startup to a thin host shell
steps.description: Refactor startup paths so orchestrator, if still needed, mainly launches or hosts Server V2 instead of reproducing runtime and product behavior in parallel.
successFactors: Orchestrator no longer acts as a second product control plane.
Remaining startup logic is thin and explicit.
The desktop app or CLI can launch one main server process in the target path.

steps.name: Move managed tool and config injection under Server V2
steps.description: Absorb orchestrator-owned managed OpenCode tool/config mutation behavior into Server V2 so these workspace capabilities are owned by the main server.
successFactors: Managed tool injection is not orchestrator-only anymore.
The server owns product-facing config mutation for these capabilities.
The migration reduces duplicate config-writing logic.

steps.name: Move router enablement policy fully into the server
steps.description: Remove any remaining orchestrator-first or app-first router enablement decisions so the server runtime model is the single authority for when router should run.
successFactors: Router enablement is server-owned.
Host shells do not make separate product decisions about messaging capabilities.
The behavior matches the server-owned router state model.

steps.name: Integrate host and sandbox launch triggers with Server V2
steps.description: For any remaining Docker, Apple container, or detached host flows, make the launched runtime graph center on Server V2 so those modes do not preserve the old orchestration architecture.
successFactors: Host and sandbox modes still converge on one main server API surface.
Container launch code is separated from product behavior ownership.
Any residual shell-only setup is explicit and small.

steps.name: Migrate desktop reconnect and status flows away from orchestrator snapshots
steps.description: Point desktop reconnect, status, and runtime-info flows at Server V2 and its DB-backed registry instead of relying on orchestrator auth or state snapshot files.
successFactors: Desktop reconnect relies on server-owned state where appropriate.
Status surfaces read from the main server.
Orchestrator state files stop being the canonical runtime source for migrated flows.

steps.name: Deprecate or remove duplicate daemon routes
steps.description: As Server V2 replacements land, remove or clearly deprecate the parallel daemon or control-plane routes so they do not linger as a second API model.
successFactors: Duplicate route families are not left active without reason.
Deprecation or removal is explicit and traceable.
Clients have a clear canonical control surface.

steps.name: Add local host-mode integration tests
steps.description: Write integration coverage for the local host-mode path where the app or CLI launches Server V2 and exercises the absorbed runtime control behavior.
successFactors: Local host mode is tested end to end.
Absorbed orchestrator control routes are covered.
The tests catch regressions in startup and runtime control.

steps.name: Add remote-connect integration tests
steps.description: Write tests for configuring a remote server, discovering remote workspaces, and routing operations through the local canonical server model.
successFactors: Remote connectivity is validated through the new architecture.
Workspace/server mapping behavior is asserted.
The tests prove the app can stay workspace-first even with remote backends.

steps.name: Add degraded-runtime handling tests
steps.description: Cover failure and degraded cases where local runtime pieces are unavailable or remote connections fail so the new control surface handles non-happy paths predictably.
successFactors: Failure states are represented through Server V2.
The app and CLI receive clear typed errors or degraded status responses.
Residual orchestrator-only recovery behavior is visible if it still exists.

steps.name: Document any residual host-shell responsibilities
steps.description: If some host-only concerns still cannot collapse into Server V2 yet, record them explicitly in the learnings or open questions files so Phase 10 can make an intentional cleanup decision.
successFactors: Remaining host-only responsibilities are named explicitly.
Future cleanup work does not have to rediscover why something stayed outside the server.
The list is small enough to evaluate for final cutover.

steps.name: Confirm the canonical runtime graph
steps.description: End the phase by verifying that the practical runtime model is app or CLI -> one main server -> supervised local dependencies, with any exceptions explicitly documented.
successFactors: The canonical runtime graph matches the target architecture.
No hidden second product control plane remains for the migrated flows.
Phase 9 leaves Phase 10 with a clear cutover target.
